prompt:
The table below shows the average number of visits made to a health centre per person in one year, by age group and type of area, in one region in 2023.

Summarise the information by selecting and reporting the main features, and make comparisons where relevant.
instruction_line: You should spend about 20 minutes on this task. Write at least 150 words.

visual.title: Visits to a health centre per person per year, by age group and area, 2023
visual.alt: A table showing the number of health centre visits per person per year for four age groups across three types of area, and the average across all three areas.

key_points: The clearest pattern is the rise with age: the 65-and-over group has the highest average across all three areas at 7.8 visits a year, while the 18-39 group has the lowest at 2.1 — a difference of roughly four times
The increase is not a straight line: there is a fall between under 18 (3.0) and 18-39 (2.1), before rising again in the 40-64 group (3.7)
The ranking of area types is the same for all four age groups: city areas highest, small towns in the middle, country areas lowest
The gap between city and country areas is widest among the elderly (8.6 vs 6.8; 1.8 visits) and narrowest for those under 18 (3.2 vs 2.8; 0.4 visits)
The single highest figure is the 65-and-over group in city areas (8.6), and the single lowest is the 18-39 group in country areas (1.7); the difference between them is more than fivefold
The final column is the average of the three area types, not their total
common_mistakes: Reading through all twenty cells one by one instead of summarising the two main patterns (age up, visits up; city > town > country)
Skipping the dip in the 18-39 group and simply writing 'visits rise steadily with age'
Mistaking the average for a total ('people made 3.0 visits in total')
Explaining causes or making recommendations ('more health centres should be built in the countryside')
Rounding decimal figures until two cells look equal and losing the comparison
